observed_effect: The bounded cost check produced a reproducible, independently verified classification and, more importantly, exposed a material cost-model defect that changes the interpretation of every prior cost-sensitivity claim. Under the repository's existing cost model the momentum edge is retained at all three lookbacks (COST_ROBUST; 5-6/10 assets; retention 0.99-1.00), but the model prices every fill at close + slippage for buys and sells alike, so sell-side slippage is favorable and a slippage-only round trip ends exactly at initial equity. The 'conservative' level therefore scales a non-adverse charge, and the COST_ROBUST label is an upper bound rather than evidence of conservative-cost robustness. The a-priori MIXED/COST_FRAGILE prediction was refuted for this cost-model reason, not because a robust net edge was demonstrated. MSFT's lookback-5 COST_FRAGILE label was traced to a null-dispersion change with unchanged candidate medians, a verdict-machinery artifact already documented for longer-horizon momentum.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe, judged against a cost-matched coin-flip null.
uncertainty_reduced: Reduced on the narrow question: the edge is retained under the repository's existing cost model (COST_ROBUST at lookbacks 3/5/10, 5-6/10 assets, retention 0.99-1.00), and the artifact is reproducible and independently verified. Not reduced on the decision-relevant question: genuinely conservative-cost robustness remains UNVERIFIED because the existing model's sell-side slippage is favorable (a slippage-only round trip ends at initial equity; AMZN slippage-only total return +5.539447 vs zero +5.537258). The a-priori prediction was refuted for a cost-model reason, not because the edge was shown to be robust.
research_result: Research/simulation only; no live trading or production execution, and no claim about live-market profitability. The short-horizon momentum edge is retained under the repository's existing cost model: COST_ROBUST at all three lookbacks (6/10 assets at lookback 3, 5/10 at 5, 5/10 at 10), 16/30 cells COST_ROBUST, median retention 0.99-1.00, and the zero-cost column exactly reproduces momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json for all 10 tickers x 3 lookbacks. The independent verifier reproduces every median, null median, segment list, n_folds, verdict, cost class, and universe verdict. However, the result does not establish conservative-cost robustness: the engine prices every fill at close + slippage, so sell-side slippage is favorable, a slippage-only round trip ends at exactly initial equity for both long and short, and on AMZN the slippage-only total return (+5.539447) slightly exceeds the zero-cost return (+5.537258) while realistic (+5.518392) is essentially commission-only (+5.516203). The 'conservative' grid level therefore does not stress the candidate. MSFT's lookback-5 COST_FRAGILE label is a null-dispersion artifact (candidate medians unchanged to four decimals; null dispersion 0.008121 -> 0.003300), not a cost effect. No claim of conservative-cost robustness is made.
